remaining_literals.value:
Choose a JCode extension (.jext) or a VS Code extension (.vsix). Which one it is comes from what is inside the file, so a package saved under any name still lands where it belongs.

Neither is verified by the marketplace and both run code in the Linux runtime, so import one only from a publisher you trust.

From a .vsix, JCode runs the part of the VS Code API that extensions built around a webview use — a side panel, commands, settings, and the current file and theme. Extensions that add languages, themes, snippets, debuggers or tasks will not work: JCode has its own systems for those, and you will be told what is missing, both on import and if it is asked for while running.

2. Finish pending dpkg configuration, if any.
3. Download reviewed packages with apt signature/hash verification.
4. Keep installed requested versions; apt may configure required dependencies.
5. Run a compile/interpreter smoke test, then atomically configure the native QuickRun environment."
